deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page records the fitting of a new suspension apparatus to the Göttingen magnetometer on 1 June (most likely 1834/35). This page, headed 'Grosse Schwingungen Jun. 1.', is a timing run of the needle swinging through a very large arc. The main purpose that can be shown from the numbers is to fix the oscillation time from a long series of transits. The page may also bear on how the period depends on amplitude and how the arc dies away.

(A) Transit times. Column 1 gives the swing number n. The next columns give the clock time t_n (h, min, s) of the n-th passage, with hours and minutes written only when they change. Swings are numbered without a break from n=1 (8h20'52.4) to n=2677 (21h44'58.26). Only short groups are written down: 1-33, 65-68, 118-121, 190-196, 264-269, 398-402, 525-529, 598-602, 2254-2258, 2532-2535 and 2675-2677.

Successive differences (my computation) show the large-amplitude effect clearly:
- t2-t1 = 44.7 s
- then 39.8, 36.8, 35.1, 33.8, 32.7, 31.8, 31.1, 30.4, ... s
- about 24.4 s at n=33
- 21.6 s at n=65-68
- 19.9 s at n=118-121
- 18.9 s at n=190-196
- 18.4 s at n=264-269
- 17.95-18.06 s at n=398-402
- about 17.8 s at n=525-602
- 17.60-17.66 s at n=2254-2677

The swing time therefore falls from about 2.5 times its small-arc value to a limit near 17.65 s. For a pendulum-type equation, T(α) = T0·(2/π)·K(sin(α/2)). The initial ratio of about 2.5 means α began near 170-175°, so the bar was nearly overturning (my inference).

(B) Reduction ('Reducirt mit 17.655'). Gauss takes T = 17.655 s and, for each late transit, forms the epoch of a fictitious swing 0:
E_n = t_n - n·17.655.
The middle column lists these epochs, written once in full as 8h37'16.130 (written '37.16.130') and then only as the last three decimals.

Group n=2254-2258 (t = 19h40'30.50, 48.10, 41'5.70, 23.36, 41.16):
- E = 8h37'16.130, .075, .020, .025, .170.

Group n=2532-2535 (21h2'18.22, 35.86, 53.62, 3'11.30):
- E = 15.760, .745, .850, .875.

Group n=2675-2677 (21h44'23.02, 40.64, 58.26):
- E = 15.895, .860, .825.

All eleven values check exactly; for example 70830.50 - 2254·17.655 = 31036.13 s = 8h37m16.13s.

The group means are 16.084, 15.8075 and 15.860 s. The near-constancy confirms T ≈ 17.655 s over the last ~420 swings, with residual drifts of a few tenths of a second.

My derivation, not on the page: the slope from groups 1 to 2 gives T ≈ 17.654 s, and from groups 1 to 3 gives T ≈ 17.6544 s. The fictitious epoch also shows that the slow early large swings 'lost' about 1000 s relative to small-arc swings: 8h37'33.8 versus the actual 8h20'52.4 for n=1.

(C) Right-hand table. It has rows (2260, 299.7, 132.0), (2537, 291.0, 52.45) and (2679, 284.3, 39.95). These are swing numbers with what appear to be scale readings and the arc (in scale divisions), which decreases 132.0 → 52.45 → 39.95. They presumably serve the damping, or the reduction to infinitely small arcs. Under one reading of the third column as the full arc, the second and third rows give a centre near 264.5 scale divisions; the first row does not fit this.

The isolated number 0.0025782 could not be reproduced with confidence; it may be a decrement or arc-correction coefficient. For comparison:
- natural log decrement 2260 → 2679: ln(132/39.95)/419 = 0.00285
- 2537 → 2679: 0.00192
- 2260 → 2537: 0.00333
None equals 0.0025782. Its meaning is left open.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: all eleven reduced epochs E_n = t_n - 17.655 n agree with the page to the last digit.
The raw transit times contain small scatter: late swing intervals range 17.60-17.80 s, e.g. 2258-2257 = 17.80 against 17.60 just before. This is observational, not a computational slip.
The derivation of 0.0025782 and the exact meaning of the columns 299.7/291.0/284.3 are not recoverable from the page alone. They are not flagged as errors, only as unverified.

results.what: Timing series of magnetometer transits at very large amplitude, showing the swing time falling from about 44.7 s to about 17.65 s as the arc decays.
results.modern_name: Amplitude dependence of the period of a physical pendulum (complete elliptic integral K), with damped oscillation.
results.usually_credited_to: Pendulum large-amplitude theory: Euler, Lagrange, Legendre (18th century). Magnetometer methodology: Gauss (Intensitas, 1832/33; Resultate des magnetischen Vereins, 1836ff).

results.what: Reduction of the transits to a fictitious epoch of swing 0 with an assumed period (E_n = t_n - n·17.655) to check and refine the oscillation time.
results.modern_name: Linear ephemeris / O−C (observed minus computed) analysis of a periodic phenomenon.
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical practice; used by Gauss and Weber in the magnetic observations.

results.what: Arc readings at swings 2260, 2537 and 2679 (132.0, 52.45, 39.95), presumably for the decrement or the reduction to infinitely small arcs.
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement of damped oscillations; small-arc correction of the period.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine laboratory record from Gauss's Göttingen magnetometer work: transit times, an O−C-style reduction with a trial period, and arc readings. The methods are exactly those Gauss and Weber published in the 1830s. The near-overturning amplitude is a nice experimental detail but involves nothing mathematically new.

transcription_corrections: '37.16.130' is a time: 8h37m16.130s, the reduced epoch of fictitious swing 0. The following '075, 020, 025, .170, 15.760, 745, 850, 875, 15.895, .860, .825' are abbreviated seconds of the same epoch for swings 2255-2258, 2532-2535 and 2675-2677 respectively.
Right-hand table first entry: '22' faint plus a bold overwritten '60', i.e. 2260; '2537' has the last digit overwritten.
'Reducirt mit 17.655' should read 'Reducirt mit 17s655', i.e. reduced with an oscillation time of 17.655 seconds.
